documents.title: Gastroenterology Consultation
documents.author: gastroenterology
documents.body:
Outside gastroenterology consultation, seen 01/27/2022, at the request of his primary care physician.

Reason: dysphagia.

HPI: Half a year of difficulty swallowing, mostly with solid food. Occasionally brings back undigested food, more often when lying flat. Describes something like a lump in the throat; his wife notes bad breath. Liquids pass. He has IPF diagnosed by pulmonology last summer, COPD on 2 L oxygen, and compensated alcohol-related cirrhosis followed by our hepatology colleagues.

Meds: tiotropium, salmeterol, albuterol nebs PRN, home O2 2 L, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 25, metformin 1000 bid. NKDA.

Exam: No neck mass on palpation. Cranial nerves and the rest of the neurological exam normal.

Barium esophagram (performed with this visit): posterior outpouching of the esophagus arising just above the upper esophageal sphincter, consistent with a Zenker diverticulum. Remainder of the esophagus passes contrast normally.

Assessment: Zenker diverticulum, symptomatic.

Plan: We discussed flexible endoscopic septotomy versus surgical options. Given his lung disease and oxygen requirement, he prefers to avoid sedation and a procedure for now, which is reasonable while he is maintaining his weight. Small bites, chew thoroughly, follow solids with liquids, stay upright for an hour after meals and avoid eating late. Return if he loses weight, has choking spells or recurrent chest infections.

Gastroenterology

documents.title: Pulmonology Follow-up
documents.author: pulmonology
documents.body:
Pulmonology follow-up, 02/22/2022.
IPF and COPD on 2 L. Breathlessness and dry cough about as they were in August. No exacerbations. Resting saturation adequate on 2 L. Bibasilar crackles, clubbing unchanged.
New Zenker diverticulum per GI - aspiration precautions reviewed.
Plan: continue oxygen and inhalers; antifibrotics remain off the table because of the liver; HRCT in late summer; return 6 months. NKDA.
Pulmonology

Exam: sat as charted on 2 L. Bibasilar crackles. Heart regular. No edema. No jaundice.

RTC June for wellness visit.

documents.title: MRI Abdomen with and without Contrast (Liver Protocol)
documents.author: radiology
documents.body:
MRI abdomen, multiphase liver protocol, 01/10/2023.
Indication: cirrhosis, new lesion on surveillance ultrasound.
Findings: Cirrhotic liver morphology. Single 2.1 cm observation in segment VI with nonrim arterial phase hyperenhancement, nonperipheral washout on portal venous and delayed phases, and an enhancing capsule. No other observations. Hepatic and portal veins patent without tumor in vein. No ascites. Spleen, pancreas, adrenals and kidneys unremarkable. No adenopathy.
Impression: 2.1 cm segment VI observation, LI-RADS 5 (definitely hepatocellular carcinoma). No vascular invasion.

documents.title: Hepatology Consultation - New HCC
documents.author: hepatology
documents.body:
Hepatology visit 01/19/2023.
Mr. Lindqvist's surveillance ultrasound in December showed a new right-lobe lesion. MRI on 1/10 characterizes it as a single 2.1 cm segment VI LI-RADS 5 observation without vascular invasion. AFP 18 ng/mL, up from 4-5 previously.

Assessment: hepatocellular carcinoma, single lesion within Milan criteria, in compensated alcohol-associated cirrhosis (Child-Pugh A). Abstinent four years.

Plan:
1. Percutaneous microwave ablation with interventional radiology - referral placed.
2. Referral to the transplant center for liver transplant evaluation. We were frank with him that his pulmonary fibrosis and oxygen need will weigh heavily in their decision.
3. MRI and AFP about 3 months after ablation.

Medications reviewed. NKDA.
Hepatology

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Primary Care Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with Ingrid after hepatology visit. MRI: single 2.1 cm HCC in segment VI, no vascular invasion; AFP 18. Hepatology plans microwave ablation and a transplant referral. We talked through what each step means. He asked whether drinking caused this; told him cirrhosis is the soil for it and that his 4 years sober matter for the transplant team. He is hopeful but realistic about his lungs.

Also: Ingrid pointed out a spot on his right upper back that she thinks has been getting bigger over the past year. Doesn't hurt or itch.

Exam: Pearly raised nodule on the R upper back, roughly 1.5 cm, with a small central crust. No other lesions noted on the back. Lungs - basal crackles as before. No jaundice, no ascites.

A/P
1. HCC - per hepatology, ablation pending; transplant referral placed by them. Labs today.
2. Back lesion - looks like a basal cell; referred to dermatology.
3. IPF/COPD, HTN, DM - unchanged.
RTC 3-4 months or sooner.

events.reason: Slowly enlarging lesion on right upper back

documents.title: Dermatology Consultation
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology consult, seen 02/03/2023.
CC: lesion right upper back.
HPI: Over the past year a spot on his right upper back has slowly grown. No pain or itching. History notable for idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and a Zenker diverticulum, both diagnosed in the past two years, COPD on oxygen and cirrhosis with a recently found liver cancer. Former smoker; years of outdoor construction work.
Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: Right upper back - 1.5 cm flesh-colored nodule with a pearly sheen, surface telangiectasias, a raised rolled border and central ulceration. No lymphadenopathy in the cervical, axillary or supraclavicular regions. Full skin exam otherwise unremarkable.

Assessment: clinically consistent with basal cell carcinoma.
Plan: shave biopsy performed today after informed consent, hemostasis with aluminum chloride, wound care reviewed. Will call with pathology and arrange excision.
Dermatology

reports.text: Specimen: skin, right upper back, shave biopsy. Microscopic: nests of basaloid cells with peripheral palisading and retraction artifact, arising from the epidermis and extending into the dermis. Overlying ulceration. Tumor present at the deep margin.
reports.conclusion: Basal cell carcinoma, nodular type. Extends to the deep margin.

documents.title: Dermatology result call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Dermatology office called: back biopsy is a nodular basal cell carcinoma. Excision scheduled 3/2 at their office. Path report scanned. Pt informed by derm.

reports.text: Specimen: skin, right upper back, excision with 4 mm margins. Residual nodular basal cell carcinoma at the biopsy site. Peripheral and deep margins free of tumor; closest margin 3 mm.
reports.conclusion: Residual basal cell carcinoma, nodular type, completely excised. Margins clear.

documents.title: Dermatology Excision Note
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body: Excision 03/02/2023, right upper back, biopsy-proven nodular BCC. Local anesthesia with lidocaine with epinephrine. Elliptical excision with 4 mm margins, layered closure. Tolerated well sitting upright on his oxygen. Pathology: margins clear. Sutures out in 14 days with your nurse or ours. Annual skin checks advised. NKDA.

documents.title: Microwave Ablation - Interventional Radiology
documents.author: interventional radiology
documents.body:
Outside interventional radiology procedure report, 03/09/2023.
Procedure: CT- and ultrasound-guided percutaneous microwave ablation, segment VI hepatocellular carcinoma (2.1 cm).
Anesthesia: general anesthesia with anesthesiology, chosen after discussion with pulmonology; extubated in the procedure suite, back on 2 L by recovery.
Technique: single antenna placed through a right intercostal approach; one ablation cycle covering the lesion with a 5 to 10 mm margin. Track ablated on withdrawal.
Post-ablation imaging: ablation zone encompasses the target; no hemorrhage or pneumothorax.
Complications: none. Discharged home the same evening.
Follow-up: multiphase MRI and AFP in about 3 months. NKDA.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Suture Removal
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Sutures removed from R upper back excision site per derm instructions. Wound well approximated, no redness or drainage. Adhesive strips applied. He also had the liver ablation last week, feels sore on the right side when he coughs, otherwise fine.

documents.title: Transplant Center Evaluation Letter
documents.author: transplant hepatology
documents.body:
Transplant hepatology, initial evaluation 04/10 and 04/20/2023.
Mr. Lindqvist is a 71-year-old man with alcohol-associated cirrhosis, abstinent since January 2019, and a single 2.1 cm hepatocellular carcinoma treated with microwave ablation on 3/9/2023. Child-Pugh A.
Comorbidities of concern: idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis and COPD on continuous oxygen 2 L; type 2 diabetes; hypertension.
Status: liver transplant evaluation opened. Candidacy cannot be decided until formal pulmonary assessment (our transplant pulmonologist) and cardiac testing are complete; these are being scheduled. He is awaiting the completion of his evaluation and is not listed.
Social work and addiction medicine review: sustained abstinence, strong support from his wife.
We will update you after committee review. NKDA.
Transplant Hepatology
